L4.S1 STRUCTURAL: eval_encoding_entropy bin count 8->64 then 64->256. 10-run (bins=64) encoding_entropy 0.0213->0.0107 (DROPPED); 3-run probe bins=256 -> 0.0080 (dropped further). Root cause: normalization denominator log2(bins^dim) = dim*log2(bins) scales linearly with log2(bins), but raw Shannon entropy is capped by log2(n_unique_samples) ≈ log2(~17 effective tuples) ≈ 4 bits regardless of bin count. Widening bins inflates the denominator without changing numerator. Xi signatures themselves (not the quantization) are the structural cap — ~300 corpus samples collapse into ~17 unique bin-tuples even at bins=8. REVERTED both probes. Finding: encoding_entropy is a DEAD metric under current eval architecture; a fix requires either (a) normalizing by log2(min(bins^dim, n_samples)) or (b) fixing the xi encoder to produce a flatter distribution. Out of scope for this batch.
